summary: Round 1's fixes do what they set out to do. The record write now merges into the file as it stands, `defer`'s temp files are cleaned on every exit, the 'nothing ships' wordings are read, a title that cleans to nothing gives way, and the fix-diff, phase and push-off prompt wordings are corrected. Two new correctness findings sit in the R1-10 fix itself (R2-14, R2-15): isDeferral still infers a decided call's deferral from stray resolve entries and from the latest resolve's tasks. Most of the remaining findings come from the same trust of agent output, in duplicate or missing deferred entries (R2-12, R2-13), with a few wording, refactor and cost nits. This repository has no scheduled commands or queued jobs, so there is no overlap to check, and the reviewer's guard refuses `node`, so the loop findings were traced through the cited lines rather than run.

findings.title: A failed mktemp or mv in defer_record after the create exits without naming the issue just opened
findings.description: redline-gh.sh runs under `set -euo pipefail` (line 153). In issue mode, `defer` opens the issue (`gh issue create`, about line 624) and then calls defer_record. defer_record runs `mkdir -p` (191), `cat` (193), `mktemp` (195) and `mv` (200) with no handling of their own. If any of them fails, set -e ends the script with only that tool's message. The issue URL is never printed or recorded. Only the jq branch (196-198), which round 1's fixes added, names the entry it could not record, including the issue. When that happens the workflow stops at `defer`, and a resume of `file deferred r<n>` falls back to the body search, which the script and the PR body call best effort. A search that lags can open a second issue. Conditions: the record's folder stops being writable, or the disk fills, between the agent's Write of the draft into that same folder and the script's write. Traced, not run. The unguarded mktemp and mv after the create were already in defer_record at 1dc6048 (its `tmp="$(mktemp ...)"` and `mv "$tmp" "$1"`). Round 1's fixes only renamed the variable and added the jq branch, so the cause predates them.
findings.proposedFix: Name the entry on every failure after the create: run defer_record's mkdir, mktemp and mv under one check (`if ! defer_tmp="$(mktemp ...)" || ...; then echo "...not recorded: $3" >&2; exit 1; fi`), or print the entry to stderr before defer_record runs. Add a gh-test.sh case with a read-only record folder after the create that expects the issue URL on stderr.

findings.title: A backslash-u escape in a draft can be decoded by the GitHub agent's Write, breaking the title check or making a live @mention
findings.description: The GitHub agent gets each draft's `content` inside a JSON block in its prompt and writes it with the Write tool (deferPrompt, workflows/redline-loop.js:2212). If the agent's Write call decodes a literal backslash-u escape that sits in the shaper's text, two things can follow. In the title, an escaped newline becomes a real line break: line 2 of the draft is then not empty, `defer` exits 2 here on every attempt, and a resume replays the same content. In the body, an escaped `@` becomes a live `@` after postedText has run, so a mention that postedText would have neutralised gets through. I tried it once from this session with the Write tool. It kept a backslash-u-000a escape literal but turned a backslash-u-0040 escape into `@`. So the decoding happens, but whether the GitHub agent does it depends on how the model writes the tool parameter. The repository cannot show that. draftTitle (workflows/redline-loop.js:1263) removes real control characters only, not their escaped spelling. #88 tracks mentions in inline comment text and replies. It does not cover issue drafts or the Write path.
findings.proposedFix: Neutralise the escape spelling before the content reaches the agent. In draftTitle and in the body fields, replace a backslash followed by `u` and four hex digits with an inert form, or have redline-gh.sh defer check the title line after the Write and report a decoded control character as such.
findings.wouldConfirm: Run the defer operation with a draft whose title contains a literal backslash-u-000a escape and whose body contains backslash-u-0040, then check the written issue-<id>.md with od -c.

findings.title: Print mode puts draft.body in a fenced block without saying the fence must be longer than any backtick run in the body
findings.description: The `done` section (line 264), and the `capped` section that round 1's R1-6 fix copied it into (line 268), say to print `draft.body` "in a fenced block, both exactly as given". A draft body can contain a triple-backtick fence. postedText leaves code spans as written, and the shaper's `found` can quote code. A plain three-backtick fence then closes early, and the rest of the body renders as markdown in the session. The person copies a broken body into their tracker. The cause is the `done` section's wording from this PR. The capped section only repeats it.
findings.proposedFix: Say the fence is one backtick longer than the longest backtick run in the body (or use a tilde fence when the body holds backticks), in both the `done` and `capped` sections.

findings.title: The default deferAt 'round' makes a headless guided run that defers anything end at a hand-off
findings.description: deferAt defaults to 'round' (line 199), so raisesDrafts is true on guided (3551). A round with one shaper deferral and no judgment call now returns a 'decisions' hand-off at 3603-3605. Before this PR the same headless `claude -p` guided run, with nothing to ask, finished. `defer at end` does not avoid the stop either. It moves it to the end-of-run stop (holdsDrafts, 3552; heldStop, 3346), so only autopilot runs headless with no stop. This is the stop the PR adds on purpose: docs/running.md, "When you are asked", says "That is the stop this setting adds to a guided run". A headless guided run already stopped at any judgment call. Two readings: either a guided run is meant to stop for drafts whatever the session (as designed), or a headless session, which can answer nothing, is meant to finish when nothing but drafts is open. The docs on headless runs (docs/running.md, Saved launch settings, The words; SKILL.md line 79) talk only about launch settings, not this stop.
findings.proposedFix: If the design stands, add one sentence to docs/running.md (Saved launch settings, The words) and SKILL.md line 79: a headless guided run that defers anything stops at the draft stop, so use autopilot headless. Otherwise file drafts as drafted in a headless session.

findings.title: issueDraft writes a Where line of '(no file):<line>' for a coverage finding minted with no file
findings.description: A coverage candidate the reviewer did not account for is minted with `file: c.file || NO_FILE`, where NO_FILE is '(no file)' (1732, 1849). issueDraft's Where line tests only `f && f.file` (1282), and '(no file)' is truthy. If such a finding is deferred, the filed issue's body reads ``- **Where:** `(no file):0` `` (or `:undefined` when the candidate gave no line), a place that does not exist. Traced through 1849 and 1282.
findings.proposedFix: Write the Where line only when `f.file && f.file !== NO_FILE` (and a line is given), and add a loop-test case that defers a minted finding with no file.

findings.title: shipsNothing ignores a task the shaper planned for its own deferral, so that task's commits are zeroed
findings.description: `planned` comes only from the round's resolve output (plannedTask, 3679, passed at 3904). The shaper's own plan is never read: shaped.findings[].files, which the schema calls "the paths the finding's task would touch" (816). If the shaper defers a finding with an empty mitigation but plans a task with files for it, and the implementer commits that task as `redline: <id> ...`, then outcomesFor sets shipsNothing true (2885) and gives the finding `commits: []`. The reply says only `deferred to #N.`, the finding is left out of `fixed` (3973), and if that is the round's only change, fixedAny is false (4793). The run then hands off with that commit never re-reviewed and no final nit pass. Conditions: the shaper contradicts its rule 6 ("only a deferral that ships a mitigation has a task", agents/redline-shaper.md:28), and the implementer commits despite being told that such a deferral has no task (2114). Traced. The loop test's empty-mitigation scenarios pin the same zeroing for a commit that only names the id. Round 1's R1-10 fix added `planned` for resolve tasks only; the shaper part was already in this PR's code at 1dc6048.
findings.proposedFix: Treat a shaper deferral whose finding lists files as planned (`planned` also takes `shaped.findings.filter(f => f.disposition === 'defer' && (f.files || []).length)`), or have vetShape warn on a deferral with an empty mitigation and files.

findings.title: A dropped draft has two representations with different reply wording
findings.description: A dropped shaper deferral becomes `droppedOutcome`, with `draftDropped: true` (2918-2919). describeOutcome then writes `<notes> No issue was opened. Mitigated in X.` (2942). A dropped deferral the person chose keeps its decided outcome, with `dropped: true` (2895). It is closed by draftClose as `<notes> Applied in X. No issue was opened.` (2927, 2944). settleHeld picks between the two again at 3395. One person action therefore reads two ways, depending on who deferred the item, and four places (outcomesFor, droppedOutcome, draftClose/describeOutcome, settleHeld) have to stay in step by hand.
findings.proposedFix: Use one flag and one wording path for a dropped draft, for example draftDropped on both, worded by describeOutcome alone.

findings.title: A revise-only pass over a review that was never posted opens real issues while its replies are file-only
findings.description: fileDeferred picks issue mode from `deferTo === 'github' && postToGitHub` (3283) and ignores record.reviewPosted. In `/redline:redline-revise <pr> round N` without `dry run`, over a round whose review is not on GitHub, has-review exits 1 and the skill sets `revise.posted = false` (skills/redline-revise/SKILL.md:24). The workflow sets `reviewPosted: false` (4632), so replyEntry routes every reply file-only, but `defer issue` still opens issues. Each issue's last line names a round and a finding (`Deferred from pull request #N by Redline (round 1, finding R1-4)`) whose review and thread are not on the PR. The commits are pushed in the same pass, since push is on. Two readings: a non-dry-run revise is a GitHub run, so opening issues is consistent with its push; or an issue should not point at a review that was never posted, and the mode should follow reviewPosted. docs/running.md, Filing, says only a dry run opens nothing.
findings.proposedFix: Either pass `postToGitHub && record.reviewPosted` into the mode, or state in docs/running.md (Filing) that a revise-only pass over an unposted review still opens issues.

findings.title: settleHeld makes two sequential GitHub-agent calls per round that held drafts
findings.description: settleHeld loops over rounds (3381). For each round with held drafts it awaits `file deferred r<n>` (3388) and then `deferred replies r<n>` (3413), one after another. A three-round run at `defer at end` with drafts in every round makes six model-backed calls in Finish, in series. Each defer entry already names its own record and command, and each reply names its own file, so the calls could be batched across rounds. This is a cost, not a defect.
findings.proposedFix: Gather every round's toFile into one defer call (each entry keeps its record file) and every round's replies into one push-and-reply call, then split the results back per round.

findings.title: settleHeld rebuilds revise()'s reply-and-post block by hand, without withAnswers and mergeThreadReplies
findings.description: settleHeld builds its replies at 3409 as replyEntry plus carriedReplies, runs push-and-reply at 3413, raises its own error, and keeps record.files and the reply ids (3416-3420). revise() does the same at 3938-3950, and wraps the replies in withAnswers and mergeThreadReplies. The two copies already differ. That is safe today only because a human pass never holds drafts: raisesDrafts is true for pass.human (3551), so holdsDrafts is false. A later change to how revise() composes replies has to be made in both places.
findings.proposedFix: Extract one helper (pass, record, findings, outcomes, doPush, why, label) that both call, with withAnswers and mergeThreadReplies applied in it.

findings.title: vetShape's comment still says 'the seven checks' after this PR added an eighth
findings.description: vetShape's comment (3506) says "then the seven checks". On main there were seven calls (checkDispositions, checkSecondLook, checkCalls, checkSpec, forceAskRules, checkDeclineReasons, checkWhy). This PR added checkDrafts (3523), so vetShape now makes eight.
findings.proposedFix: Change "the seven checks" to "the eight checks" in the comment above vetShape.

findings.title: Two shaper deferred entries for one finding become two drafts, two filings and two Deferred lines
findings.description: Nothing collapses duplicate `deferred` entries for one id. checkDispositions keeps every entry whose id is deferred (2999-3004). checkDrafts validates only the first, via `.find` (3098). draftsOf maps each entry and bumps the shared record.drafts version whenever the text differs (3559-3566). So entries A and B for R1-4 are raised at the stop as versions 1 and 2. At 3896 they are re-versioned as 3 and 4, and both go into toFile. fileDeferred gives both the same file and command. The agent writes A and opens the issue, then writes B over issue-R1-4.md, and the second defer reuses the issue. The committed draft therefore no longer matches the filed issue's body. deferredAll gets two pushes (3906), so the handoff shows `### Deferred (2)` with R1-4 twice (4139). Conditions: the shaper returns two entries for one finding, against its contract. Traced; node is refused to the reviewer, so not run.
findings.proposedFix: In checkDispositions (or checkDrafts), keep one entry per id: stop at shape on duplicates, as on a missing draft, or keep the first with a warning. Add a loop-test case whose shaper returns two entries for one id.

findings.title: A defer override the resolve agent returns no entry for is never drafted or filed, with no warning
findings.description: resolveWith refuses resolve entries that lack a draft (3663-3666). It never checks that a `defer` override, or a call answered with a deferral, got an entry at all. Scenario: plan dial, `decisions: {R1-1: {disposition: 'defer', notes: 'Defer it behind a log line.'}}`, and the resolve returns a task for R1-1 but `deferred: []`. `deferred` then holds no R1-1 entry, so isDeferral never sees it and there is no `file deferred r1` call. outcomesFor gives a decided outcome with `filed: null` (2895). The reply reads `Defer it behind a log line. Applied in 1bbbbbb (...). · decided by: @author`, result.deferred is [], and no warning is raised. The shaper's own deferrals stop at checkDrafts in this case (3096-3102); overrides do not. That breaks this PR's promise that a deferred item always ends in a drafted issue. Conditions: the resolve agent leaves out the entry its prompt (2008) and agents/redline-resolve.md:23 ask for. Traced; node is refused to the reviewer. The scenario is in /tmp/redlinerepro/reviewer-r2-scenarios.mjs.
findings.proposedFix: After resolveWith's fresh/undrafted check, stop at resolve when any newOverrides finding with `disposition === 'defer'` has no entry in `fresh` or `deferred`, with the same message shape as the undrafted error. Add a loop-test case: plan dial, defer override, resolveDeferred [] → status error, stage resolve.

findings.title: plannedTask reads only the latest resolve, so after a reshape raises a call R1-10's guard stops working
findings.description: plannedTask, added by R1-10's fix, reads `resolved.tasks` (3679). When a reshape raises a new call, `resolved` is replaced (3767) by a resolve whose prompt holds only the raised calls' decisions (resolvePrompt, 1974). Its tasks cover those calls only. Scenario (autopilot): R1-1 is a call whose first resolve returns a stray `{id: 'R1-1', mitigation: ''}` entry beside a task with files; the plan bounces; the reshape raises a call on R1-2. After `resolve r1 #2`, plannedTask('R1-1') is false. isDeferral then returns true (3693: decision, resolveDeferred has R1-1, no mitigation, no planned task), so `file deferred r1` opens an issue for R1-1. outcomesFor's `planned` set lacks R1-1 (3904), so shipsNothing is true (2885), commits are zeroed, and the reply reads `... No code change. Deferred to #301.` although R1-1's commit landed. R1-1 also drops out of `fixed`. This is R1-10's case: R1-10 was fixed, but it still reproduces once a reshape raises a call. The same replacement drops the first resolve's tasks from needCommits (3827), which predates round 1's fixes. Traced through 3679, 3693, 3767, 3896-3904 and 2885; node is refused to the reviewer. The scenario is in /tmp/redlinerepro/reviewer-r2-scenarios.mjs.
findings.proposedFix: Accumulate every resolve's tasks over the round (for example `const resolvedTasks = []`, pushed in resolveWith), and read plannedTask and needCommits from that list, not from `resolved`. Add a loop-test case: autopilot, ask R1-1 with a stray empty-mitigation resolve entry, planBounce 1, reshapeAsk R1-2 → no `file deferred r1`, and R1-1's reply says `Applied in`.

findings.title: isDeferral cannot tell a fix with a stray mitigated resolve entry from a 'mitigate' answer, so that fix is filed as an issue
findings.description: After R1-10's fix, a decided finding counts as a deferral when the resolve agent returned an entry for it and `hasMitigation(d) || !plannedTask(d.id)` (3693). A call answered with a fix, or autopilot taking a fix recommendation, whose resolve output also carries an entry with a non-empty mitigation (for example the shaper's recommendation copied over) satisfies `resolveDeferred.has(id) && hasMitigation(d)`. It is then filed as an issue with no question on autopilot, and its reply ends `Deferred to #N`. A real 'mitigate' answer has the same shape (a task and a mitigated entry), so the workflow cannot tell the two apart from what it reads. R1-10 covered only the empty-mitigation entry. Its loop-test case (`strayResolve`) uses `mitigation: ''`, and the mitigated sibling still files. Before round 1's fixes this case also filed (`Boolean(roundDecisions[d.id])`), so this was not newly introduced, but the line that decides it is the fix's. Conditions: the resolve agent returns an entry for a decision it was not asked to defer (agents/redline-resolve.md:23 asks for one only for 'mitigate' or a defer override). Traced; node is refused to the reviewer.
findings.proposedFix: Have the resolve agent return each applied decision's resulting disposition (fix, defer or accept) in its JSON, and read deferral from that rather than from stray entries and task file lists. That would also remove R2-14's dependence on `resolved`.

findings.title: The handoff's generic opening says no item was asked about after a round that asked about a fix-diff low finding
findings.description: A low-severity correctness finding with inFixDiff on a fix-diff round is in likeNit and buys nothing (3971-3972). Scenario: round 2 (fix-diff) has R2-1, low, inFixDiff true. The shaper asks about it, and the person answers 'Keep it' with no commit. bought is false and fixed is empty, so fixedAny is false (4793), and the run calls `finish('handoff', ..., handoffComment({}))` (4798). The comment opens with the fallback at 4017: "Redline ran 2 review rounds; the last one verified no new correctness item to fix or ask about." That round did ask about R2-1, and the same handoff lists it under Put to @author. Traced through 4747, 3972, 4793-4798 and 4017.
findings.proposedFix: Give handoffComment an ending for this case (for example `minorOnly`), whose sentence says the last round's correctness items were low-severity bugs in the previous round's fixes, handled like nits, so it bought no further round.

list.summary: plannedTask reads only the latest resolveWith output. After a reshape raises a new call, resolved is replaced at line 3767 by a resolve that returns tasks only for the raised calls, so the first resolve's planned tasks are forgotten and R1-10's guard in isDeferral and outcomesFor's shipsNothing stops working.
list.failure_scenario: Reproduced with the loop-test harness: autopilot; R1-1 is a call whose first resolve returns a stray entry {mitigation: ''} beside a task with files; the plan bounces and the reshape raises a new call on R1-2, so 'resolve r1 #1' runs. Result: 'file deferred r1' opens #301 for R1-1, and its reply reads 'Autopilot took the shaper's recommendation: Keep it. No code change. Deferred to #301.' although commit R1-1 landed. R1-1 is also dropped from `fixed`. The same reassignment drops the first resolve's tasks from needCommits (that part predates this branch). Fix: accumulate tasks across every resolveWith call in the round.

list.summary: Nothing checks that a person's `defer` override produced a deferred entry. resolveWith rejects entries that lack a draft, but not a defer override for which the resolve agent returned no entry, so the person's deferral is silently never drafted or filed.
list.failure_scenario: Reproduced: plan dial, decisions {R1-1: {disposition: 'defer', notes: 'Defer it behind a log line.'}}, and the resolve returns a task but deferred: []. The run ends 'done' with no 'file deferred r1' call and no warning. The reply is 'Defer it behind a log line. Applied in 1bbbbbb ... · decided by: @author' and result.deferred is []. This breaks the branch's promise that a deferred item always ends in a drafted issue. The shaper's own deferrals stop at checkDrafts in this case; overrides do not.

list.summary: Altitude: isDeferral guesses whether a decided call became a deferral from side signals (a stray resolve entry, its mitigation text, whether some resolve planned a task with files). A fix with a stray mitigated entry cannot be told apart from a 'mitigate' answer, and the guess fails whenever those signals go stale (finding 1).
list.failure_scenario: A call answered 'fix' whose resolve output also carries an entry with a non-empty mitigation (for example the shaper's recommendation copied over) satisfies resolveDeferred.has(id) && hasMitigation(d). It is filed as an issue, on autopilot with no question. Root fix: have the resolve agent return each applied decision's resulting disposition (fix, defer or accept) explicitly, and read deferral from that instead of from entries and task file lists.

list.summary: shipsNothing ignores the shaper's own planned task. For an undecided shaper deferral with an empty or 'none (...)' mitigation, `planned` holds only resolve tasks, so a mitigation task the shaper did plan (shaped.findings[].files) has its commits zeroed.
list.failure_scenario: The shaper defers R1-3 with mitigation '' but plans a task touching app/x.php, and the implementer commits 'redline: R1-3 ...'. outcomesFor gives R1-3 commits [], so the reply says only 'deferred to #N.', R1-3 is left out of `fixed`, and when it is the round's only code change fixedAny is false. The run hands off with that commit never re-reviewed and no final nit pass.

list.summary: fileDeferred picks issue mode from deferTo and postToGitHub only, not from whether the round's review is on GitHub. A revise-only pass over a review that was only written opens real issues while its replies are file-only.
list.failure_scenario: Run /redline:redline-revise <pr> round 1 without `dry run` over a round whose review was a dry run (revise.posted false). postToGitHub is true, so `defer issue` opens 'Deferred from pull request #N by Redline (round 1, finding R1-4)' on GitHub, but replyEntry routes every reply 'file-only' because reviewPosted is false. The issues point at a round and threads that do not exist on the PR.

list.summary: The handoff's fallback opening sentence is now wrong after a round whose only correctness item was a low-severity fix-diff finding put to the person and answered with no fix.
list.failure_scenario: Reproduced: round 2 (fix-diff) has R2-1, low with inFixDiff true, which the shaper asks about and the person answers 'Keep it' (no commit). likeNit means it buys nothing and fixedAny is false, so finish('handoff', {}) posts 'Redline ran 2 review rounds; the last one verified no new correctness item to fix or ask about.' even though that round did ask about R2-1.

list.summary: Duplicate deferred entries for one id are never collapsed. draftsOf maps each one, bumping the shared version on every call, so one finding becomes two drafts that are both filed and both listed.
list.failure_scenario: The shaper returns two `deferred` entries for R1-4 with different text (its rules say exactly one). checkDrafts validates only the first (.find), and checkDispositions removes no duplicates. The stop raises R1-4 twice (v1 and v2), and the final draftsOf bumps it to v3/v4, which are never shown. toFile holds two R1-4 entries: the agent opens the issue with draft A, overwrites issue-R1-4.md with draft B, and the second defer reuses the issue. The committed draft no longer matches the filed issue, and the handoff lists '### Deferred (2)' with R1-4 twice.

list.summary: The draft reaches disk through the GitHub agent's Write tool, which turns a literal backslash-u escape into the real character, so a title containing a backslash-u-000a escape becomes two lines and `defer` refuses the draft on every attempt.
list.failure_scenario: A finding about JSON escaping is titled 'Parser drops \u000a in keys'. draftTitle cleans the text, but the Write tool writes a real newline, so line 2 of issue-R2-1.md is not empty and the script exits 2 ('must open with "# <title>" and an empty line'). The round stops at stage defer, and a resume replays the same content and stops again. The same decoding can turn a backslash-u-0040 escape in the body into a live '@' that slips past postedText (the mention side is #88's class).

list.summary: After `gh issue create` succeeds, a failed mktemp or mv inside defer_record exits under set -e with only that tool's message. Only the jq-failure branch names the issue already opened (R1-3), so the URL is lost.
list.failure_scenario: The record's folder is unwritable, or the disk is full, when defer_record runs after the create: mktemp prints 'mkstemp failed' and the script exits without printing the issue URL or recording it. The workflow stops at defer, and the resume relies on the best-effort search, which can lag and open a second issue for the same finding.

list.summary: The new default deferAt 'round' adds a stop to every guided run that defers anything, including a round with no judgment call, so a headless guided run that used to finish now ends at a hand-off nobody can answer.
list.failure_scenario: `claude -p '/redline 21'` with the saved dial guided and no deferral words. Round 1 has fixes plus one deferral and no ask. Before this branch the run finished; now revise returns kind 'decisions' with drafts at line 3603, and the headless session ends with an unanswered handoff marker. Only typing `defer at end` or autopilot avoids it.

list.summary: issueDraft writes a Where line for a coverage-minted finding with no file, so the filed issue reads '(no file):0'.
list.failure_scenario: A finding minted with NO_FILE (line 0) is deferred, and the GitHub issue body shows '- **Where:** `(no file):0`'. The guard tests only f.file's truthiness, and '(no file)' is truthy.

list.summary: Print mode puts draft.body in a fenced block, but bodies routinely hold code spans and can hold a triple-backtick fence, which closes the block early.
list.failure_scenario: With deferTo print, a draft whose `found` quotes a code block containing ``` ends the printed fence partway through. The rest renders as markdown, and the person pastes a mangled body into their tracker. A fence longer than any run of backticks in the body avoids this.

list.summary: Efficiency: settleHeld makes two sequential GitHub-agent calls per round that held drafts ('file deferred r<n>', then 'deferred replies r<n>'), so the end-of-run cost grows with the number of rounds.
list.failure_scenario: A three-round run at deferAt end with drafts in each round makes six model-backed GitHub-agent calls in Finish, one after another. Each defer prompt already names its own record and command, so all rounds' drafts could go in one defer call and all held replies in one push-and-reply call.

list.summary: Reuse: settleHeld rebuilds the reply list and the push-and-reply call by hand, repeating revise()'s block (replyEntry plus carriedReplies, the run() call, the error, record.files and keepReplyIds) and silently leaving out withAnswers and mergeThreadReplies.
list.failure_scenario: The two copies already differ (no withAnswers or mergeThreadReplies in settleHeld). That is safe today only because held drafts never occur in a human pass. A later change to reply composition in revise() would have to be made twice, and if a human pass ever held drafts, a shared thread would get duplicate replies with no answers marker. A shared postReplies(pass, record, findings, outcomes, doPush, why, label) helper would remove the copy.

No issue was opened.' for a dropped person-chosen deferral. Four places (replyBody, describeOutcome, draftClose, settleHeld) must be kept consistent by hand. One flag and one wording path would cover both.

list.summary: vetShape's comment still says 'the seven checks', but the branch added checkDrafts, so there are now eight.
list.failure_scenario: A maintainer counting the checks against the comment finds eight calls and one fewer described. This is minor doc drift in the function that sets the checks' order.
